outcome: Surgical site infection (SSI) clinical presentation (wound discharge, pain, induration, fever)
Maternal morbidities (extended length of hospital stay)
cohort: The study included 153 women who developed surgical site infection following cesarean section at a tertiary care center.
finding: Intraoperative adhesions and prolonged operative time were predictors of SSI, with wound discharge being a universal clinical presentation and Staphylococcus aureus the most common causative organism.
mod_finding: The study exclusively characterized surgical site infections (SSI) occurring specifically after cesarean section, detailing their clinical presentation, causative organisms, and associated maternal morbidities.
